correctness.rationale: At each stage the lower faces carry a fixed mandatory marker (both poles, then one pole, then a_i), and every face with that marker pairs along a single pivot b_1, beta_1, alpha_1 or c_i. All remaining competing one-vertex extensions of a lower face also carry the marker and omit the pivot, so have been removed by larger lower faces. Any higher coface would force a competing one-vertex extension. The counts are respectively 2^(m-1), 2 times 3^m 2^(q-1), and the sum of 3^(i-1)5^(m-i)3^q over i=1,...,m. The last stage contracts each interval component a_i c_i to c_i, not to the empty set. The survivor join of m+q two-point factors is precisely the named crosspolytope boundary. The degree hypothesis makes the two poles intrinsic; deleting them identifies the paths by length, proving the automorphism group. The invariant pole-free inclusion is a homology isomorphism even though the chosen elementary collapse is not equivariant. On degree-zero reduced homology reversal preserves the two long-factor components and swaps the two short-factor components. Joining the difference cycles gives a generator; transposition of two factors exchanges two vertices in every joined simplex and contributes minus one. Hence the stated integral character holds.
residual_risks: Reported finite sample includes (1,1), which is outside the full-automorphism-group scope; the checks in that case concern natural symmetries only. No equivariant collapse or formal proof certificate inferred.

The three-arm analysis is relevant to all three-arm instances but does not handle the arbitrary mixed number of arms or the integral action.
